decision: Scored routes in dollars, with each priority as a price list, and simulated each leg once
why: A normalized weight changes when an unrelated route is added, and it cannot explain a trade in money

decision: Rejected on-time floors and weights that sum to 10000 basis points
why: Those weights book a route that loses cargo because a dollar of freight is not a dollar of loss
result: the report table is the shipped price list

decision: Required one set of numbers per hop, and added regret against a hindsight oracle
why: A shared hop needs one owner, and the scorecard needs a realized-cost comparison
result: hop conflicts fail parse, and Policy.ORACLE is the hindsight pick

decision: Locked the zero-noise shipment to route B under balanced prices and route A under cost-first
why: The scores are closed form, so a later change to the prose or the rank has to keep the same pick
result: balanced ships B at $11,600 and cost-first ships A at $10,600

decision: Drove the Streamlit page from shipment SHP-001 to SHP-010
why: The infeasible shipment has to report the deadline miss
result: headline switches to the deadline miss

decision: Recorded five seeds at 2000 planning draws and 1000 held-out draws
why: One seed can make the cheapest-quote penalty look larger than the catalog usually is
result: recommended regret $143 to $373, cheapest mean ratio 5.24 to 8.19

decision: Scored every schedule-feasible route and compared headlines to the freight quote and the scheduled hours
why: A Pareto veto could drop the lower dollar score, and an expected-cost headline disagreed with the quote the operator can see
result: seed 42 SHP-015 ships dominated route E, and the zero-noise headline strings still hold

decision: Accepted the dominated route as the shipment when its risk-adjusted cost is lower
why: The 21:10 row named the symptom. This row names the rule. Hop checks live in the parser, and regret lives in the oracle policy
result: SHP-015 on seed 42 ships route E while B dominates it

decision: Stated the dollar margin when a dominated route ships, and warned when that margin is under 5% of the score
why: A sentence that only says the cost is lower hides whether the gap is $546 or decisive
result: the SHP-015 sentence names $546 and the near-tie caveat

decision: Opened the Streamlit app in a browser and selected SHP-010
why: The widget test does not show the page a reviewer will open
result: headline is the 19-hour deadline miss for route B via Busan

decision: Replaced abstract rail and straight sea distances with sea-air transfers and a coarse maritime corridor graph
why: Candidate geography should be mode-compatible while remaining explicit about synthetic service assumptions
result: seed-7 catalog regenerated; prior rows describe earlier catalogs

decision: Audited fixed routes across planning seeds and held-out disruption stresses
why: Price stability does not establish sampling stability or model accuracy
result: 86.85% sampling agreement; 7 review flags; combined-stress on-time 95.17%
